verdict:
NO ENTRY - but escalate, because red's prosecution collapsed on contact and the reason the answer survives is a finding red never made.

RED'S ONE UNASSAILABLE FINDING IS ALSO THE BEST FINDING IN THE BATCH. Headline revenue of $28.8M was up 54% year over year. Cloud revenue of $23.8M 'included approximately $12.3 million associated with the previously disclosed customer termination.' Strip the break fee and organic revenue is about $16.5M against $18.7M - down roughly 11-12%. The company also booked about $2.2M of credit losses and roughly $4M payable to the GPU lease provider on the same default. So the entire growth delta, and more, is a termination fee from a customer that left and did not pay. The marketed takeaway was plus 54%, the tape paid plus 16.6% for it, and the underlying business shrank. Both venues agree on the disclosure, which is a clean VENUE-MATCH - the company disclosed the break fee plainly and it is the market that read the headline. That is a takeaway-divergence finding, and it is correct.

EVERYTHING ELSE RED BUILT, BLUE TOOK APART, AND BLUE WAS RIGHT EACH TIME.

Red's finding 3 refuted the 40MW energization using a Landsat thermal series showing declining parcel heat. But the claim under test was that full run-rate billing begins 'later in August' - a FUTURE-DATED claim at bench time. A satellite series whose latest pass precedes the claim window cannot refute it. Worse, red had written that exact guard as its own kg_candidate one finding earlier (satellite_scene_recency_guard) and then violated it in the adjacent paragraph. A bench inventing a methodological rule and breaking it in the same document is a serious self-consistency failure, and blue caught it. Blue also noted the minus 4.77 degrees per year trend is the FORMER industrial building's shutdown baseline, not evidence of a failed energization.

Red's finding 5 declared the cloud capacity leg dead because sentinel2_buildout returned activity=False at MTL-3. Blue pulled the 10-Q: WhiteFiber EXERCISED ITS PURCHASE OPTION and acquired MTL-3 outright on 2026-05-08 for CAD $24.7M. A finished building shows no construction because it is finished. Buying the asset is commitment, not retreat. This is a detector-literacy failure of a kind we will hit again, and blue's completed_asset_reads_as_paused candidate should be wired.

Red's finding 2 called the $932.9M single-tenant colo backlog uninvestable by analogy to the cloud customer that just defaulted. Concentration is real and confirmed - there is no executed credit enhancement behind Nscale, and the 'investment grade' language in the PR attaches to Nscale's customers and to future pipeline, not to this contract. But red listed 'no primary evidence of Nscale's balance-sheet capacity' as something that would change its mind, and it was checkable in minutes: Nscale raised a $1.1B Aker-led Series B, took another $433M days later, added roughly $790M of debt in May 2026, holds a $14B Microsoft and Nvidia GPU deal, and is on a 2026 IPO track. The failure mode of a small defaulting cloud customer does not transfer to a Microsoft-anchored counterparty with billions in fresh capital. Blue correctly cut this from FATAL to SIZING.

And red's finding 7 - 'prepay is not cash' - inverts the economics. The $143.1M of contract liabilities is cash ALREADY RECEIVED, and it DOUBLED from $79.6M in six months. Counterparties are wiring money in. The obligation is to deliver service, not to repay. Blue's Mode-B ground truth is the decisive piece here and red skipped it entirely: audited construction in progress went from $157.0M to $484.6M in the first half on $344.7M of capex. The buildout is financially corroborated in the audited numbers whatever the satellites did or did not see.

SO WHY IS THE ANSWER STILL NO? Because of blue's prize table, which red never built. Enterprise value is about $1.4B - roughly $1.14B of equity on 38.66M diluted shares, plus $230M of 2031 converts, plus roughly $85-95M of drawn facilities, less $56.1M of cash - against an organic run-rate of about $66M. That is roughly 21x. The Nscale contract at $865M over ten years is $86.5M a year; at a 65-75% powered-shell EBITDA margin that is $56-65M, and at 12-15x that is $0.7-1.0B for NC-1 fully performing. A fully performing anchor contract plus the existing organic business does not clear the enterprise value, let alone a plus-50% bar. That is the binding reason for no entry, and it does not depend on any satellite read.

NOW THE CONSISTENCY CHECK I OWE, BECAUSE I APPLIED THE OPPOSITE RULE TO CLSK IN THIS SAME BATCH. Blue's prize table is built on 40MW of contracted scope. I fetched the Nscale PR blue cited. It states that 'management believes the site may support up to 200 MW of total electrical supply over time, subject to infrastructure upgrades and other conditions,' that the parties 'plan for the potential expansion of this deployment toward double its initial size by the end of 2027,' and that 'Nscale will receive priority notification of future capacity availability at NC-1 before such capacity is marketed to other customers.' So the same scope-truncation pattern is present. But the severity is not the same, and the difference is instructive: CLSK's excluded scope is an EXECUTED letter of intent plus exclusivity over a specific 718 acres and 885MW, whereas WYFI's is a management BELIEF about site potential, subject to infrastructure upgrades, plus a priority-notification right that is weaker than a right of first refusal. Blue also, to its credit, named the requirement explicitly - it wrote that upside requires expansion beyond 40MW - rather than burying it. Verdict: the truncation finding fires here at reduced severity. It does not overturn blue's no-entry conclusion, but the prize table should be re-run at the doubling case (80MW by end-2027) before this name is ever re-courted, because that scenario roughly doubles the NOI leg and is the difference between 'cannot clear' and 'clears at the top of the range.'

WHAT THIS NAME ACTUALLY IS: a real buildout, financially corroborated, anchored by a well-capitalized private tenant, attached to a shrinking legacy cloud business, priced at roughly 21x organic revenue with the funded prize sitting at or below today's enterprise value. Red's terminal REJECT is too strong; blue's evidence-gated WATCH is right. The cheap resolution costs one quarter: Q3 colocation revenue is a hard, pre-committed number.
blue_ruling: PARTIALLY OVERTURNED, and severely - of red's seven findings, two were OVERTURNED outright and three REDUCED, leaving only the break-fee finding and the scene-staleness finding standing as written. Blue then supplied a BETTER reason for the same no-entry conclusion via a prize table red never built. Both benches carry 8/10. Two equally confident benches reaching the same verdict through almost entirely different evidence is the definition of a discordant record.
reopen_gates: DATA (the cleanest binary in the batch, and it is one quarter away): Q3 colocation revenue at or above $14M WITH accounts receivable flat. Colo has printed ~$4.7-4.8M for two straight quarters against a 40MW contract that must run roughly $17-21M per quarter at full rate, and management targeted full run-rate billing 'later in August'. Below ~$10-12M means NC-1 slipped or is billing under-rate. The AR condition is essential and separates billing from collecting - a colo step-up alongside an AR jump is Nscale not paying.

EVENT: an 8-K naming an EXECUTED credit enhancement, letter of credit, deposit, or parent guarantee behind the Nscale contract. The company is currently only 'actively evaluating potential investment-grade credit enhancement structures' and the 'investment grade' language in the deal PR attaches to Nscale's customers, not to this contract.

EVENT: NC-1 secured financing SIGNED on disclosed terms. It has been in exclusivity only, and management has already conceded it 'has taken longer than we initially anticipated'. It is sized to return a significant portion of the capital invested in NC-1, so signing materially changes the funding picture against $344.7M of half-year capex versus ~$60.4M of liquidity.

SCOPE (must be closed before re-court, not after): re-run the prize table at the disclosed expansion case, not the contracted case. The Nscale PR discloses a plan to expand the deployment 'toward double its initial size by the end of 2027' and management belief that the site may support up to 200MW. At 80MW the NOI leg roughly doubles and the funded-prize conclusion may invert. Grade the firmness honestly - this is a plan and a belief, not CLSK's executed exclusivity.

PHYSICAL: a post-August Landsat or Sentinel-2 pass showing a genuine thermal step at NC-1. This is now a VALID test because the claim window has opened - it was not a valid refutation before the window, which is precisely where red went wrong. Re-dispatch with a scene-recency assertion.
